subject: "Partialling out" of predictors on endogenous DVs with predict()?

messages.author: ec12e510d7b112ad
messages.subject: "Partialling out" of predictors on endogenous DVs with predict()?
parts:
Dear all,

I do have a model with 4 exogenous predictors on 4 endogenous DVs. In the second step I am analyzing the influence of those 4 endogenous DVs on to a binary outcome (0|1). Since lavaan can only handle probit regression with WLSMV yet and I really don´t want to use WLSMV (see my argument here) I try to predict latent factor scores (I know it´s actually a bad idea!) and use these factor scores for glm() . But I just saw today that the influence of the predictors on the DVs is not "out partialled" in the factor scores of the endogenous DVs. Is there any way of obtaining factor scores for the four DVs while controlling for the four predictors' influence on the DVs?

Thanks a lot!

PS: Yves, any news on logistic regression and MLR?

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: "Partialling out" of predictors on endogenous DVs with predict()?
parts:
If you want to know the effect of the DVs on the binary outcome while controlling for the IVs, then the IVs also need to be predictors of the binary outcome.  If you have the Baron & Kenny model

M ~ a*X
Y ~ b*M

then "b" is the effect of M on Y without controlling for X (thus assuming full mediation).  To control for X, you need to allow for partial mediation:

Y ~ b*M + c*X

If you want to use marginal ML and a logit link, I think that feature is available but still under development.  Check out this previous post:

https://groups.google.com/d/msg/lavaan/zDcHbOnxdRg/97k6OgvFk60J

Terry
